project.title: Claims Portal Frontend
project.description: Java/Spring service that reconciles card settlement files against the ledger nightly and raises breaks to Finance Ops. Being handed over as the lead moves to a new programme.
project.roles: Giver: tech lead, owns design, releases, on-call. Taker: senior engineer, will own delivery and support.
project.tech_stack: Java 17, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Jenkins, Docker, Kubernetes (EKS), Grafana
project.dev_env: Docker Compose locally plus shared dev namespace on EKS; secrets in HashiCorp Vault
project.test_env: Shared UAT namespace with masked prod data, refreshed monthly; Selenium and Postman suites in Jenkins
project.extra: Focus on release process, incident handling and anything that is not written down.

qa.question: What undocumented design decisions did we make for the Java 17 and Kafka reconciliation pipeline, and where are the single points of failure in our Kubernetes EKS setup?
qa.answer: We decided to process Kafka settlement events out-of-order using an aggressive local state store in Java 17, which bypasses strict ledger locks. The single point of failure in our EKS setup is the single replica Kafka Connect pod that streams PostgreSQL CDC events. If that pod drops, settlement breaks silently halt until a manual restart.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would trace a dropped card settlement message from the Kafka broker through the Spring Boot service to the PostgreSQL database in EKS.
What hidden coupling exists across our Spring Boot modules, and which custom coding standards or repo branching rules do we enforce that are missing from our README?
qa.answer: There is hidden tight coupling between the settlement-core and ledger-adaptor modules via static utility beans that violate our domain boundaries. We enforce a strict branching rule where feature branches must be squashed into a release candidate branch prefixed with rc-v2, which isn't documented in the README.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would refactor our core ledger reconciliation package in Java 17, ensuring you adhere to our internal module boundaries and pull request standards.
What manual steps or hidden HashiCorp Vault secrets are required to spin up the local Docker Compose environment that aren't captured in our shared dev EKS namespace setup?
qa.answer: To spin up Docker Compose locally, you need to manually fetch the database decryption keys from a specific restricted folder in HashiCorp Vault. These local secrets differ completely from the automated IAM role injections used in our shared dev EKS namespace.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would fetch a rotated secret from HashiCorp Vault and update the configuration for the shared dev namespace in EKS without causing downtime.
What manual overrides or undocumented approval gates exist in our Jenkins pipeline for deploying Docker images to Kubernetes EKS, and how do we handle database migrations?
qa.answer: It is mostly in my head and handled via the usual Jenkins process when the time comes. I just trigger the deployment pipeline and handle any manual gates as needed.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would execute a complete zero-downtime release using Jenkins and EKS, including the exact steps for rolling back if the PostgreSQL migration fails.
Which flaky tests in our Selenium and Postman Jenkins suites do we routinely ignore, and what manual quirks exist in the monthly UAT masked data refresh?
qa.answer: We routinely ignore three flaky Selenium UI tests related to the date-picker component in the reconciliation dashboard because of timing issues. For the monthly UAT masked data refresh, you have to manually trigger a Postgres vacuum script in Jenkins right after the dump completes to avoid deadlocks.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would diagnose a nightly test failure in the Jenkins Postman suite caused by a discrepancy in the UAT masked PostgreSQL dataset.
What undocumented vendor schema changes or strict SLAs do we have for incoming card settlement files, and where do upstream Kafka schema breaks usually manifest?
qa.answer: Card settlement files from our primary vendor frequently drop optional column fields without notice, requiring us to patch our JSON deserializers manually. Upstream Kafka schema breaks usually manifest as silent consumer thread deaths in the claims-ingestion topic rather than explicit parsing exceptions.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would investigate a missing settlement file from an upstream vendor, verify the data flow into PostgreSQL, and notify Finance Ops.
What recurring Grafana alerts wake us up at night, which unwritten runbooks do you actually use to fix them, and who is our true escalation point in Finance Ops?
qa.answer: It is mostly in my head and handled via the usual process when an alert fires at night. I just look at the Grafana dashboards and use my usual mental runbook to sort it out.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would triage a critical Grafana memory leak alert on the Java 17 pod at 2 AM, utilizing our Kubernetes logs and runbook procedures.
What unspoken expectations do the Finance Ops stakeholders have regarding ledger break thresholds, and which reporting deadlines cause the most political pressure?
qa.answer: Finance Ops expects any ledger break over fifty dollars to be flagged immediately, even though our formal SLA is set at one hundred dollars. The monthly regulatory reporting deadline on the fifth business day causes extreme political pressure if reconciliation isn't fully signed off by midnight.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would explain a high-priority ledger reconciliation break to Finance Ops stakeholders during their monthly audit sign-off meeting.
How are database credentials managed outside of HashiCorp Vault for emergency access, and what undocumented compliance audit duties must we perform quarterly?
qa.answer: For emergency database access, a break-glass root password is hardcoded in a secured KeePass file shared only among senior tech leads. Every quarter, we must manually export audit logs from PostgreSQL and cross-reference them with Jira access requests for our compliance review.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would audit our Kubernetes EKS role-based access control and revoke an expired developer token without violating compliance policies.
Which Jira tickets represent half-done tech debt that management thinks is complete, and what dangerous workarounds are currently baked into our branch?
qa.answer: Jira ticket CLAIMS-409 represents half-done multi-currency support that management thinks is fully production-ready. We currently have a dangerous SQL string concatenation workaround baked into the main reconciliation branch to handle legacy currency codes.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would prioritize our open backlog of ledger reconciliation bug fixes against incoming feature requests for the upcoming sprint.
What unwritten rules, personal workarounds, or informal Slack channels do you actually rely on to keep the Java 17 service running smoothly every night?
qa.answer: I heavily rely on an informal Slack channel called #claims-nightly-watch where senior engineers hang out to monitor job spikes. There is also an unwritten rule that you must restart the cache warmer pod fifteen minutes before the midnight batch run to prevent OOM errors.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would discover the root cause of an obscure Spring Boot startup error when Google, Confluence, and our documentation yield zero results.
Which Confluence architecture and runbook pages are hopelessly outdated, and who are the specific SMEs across infrastructure and finance we must rely on?
qa.answer: The Confluence pages detailing the disaster recovery failover steps for the settlement pipeline are hopelessly outdated and reference decommissioned Jenkins jobs. For infrastructure issues, we must rely on Dave in platform engineering, and for finance quirks, Sarah is our go-to SME.

qa.question: Walk me through how you would update our stale Confluence documentation after resolving a major incident, ensuring the right SMEs review your changes.
